draft.assessment: Severe PTSD symptoms (PCL-5 44; CAPS-5 severe) in a 76-year-old with military sexual trauma (MST), prior documented response to cognitive processing therapy (CPT), currently on sertraline with multiple comorbidities including coronary disease post-STEMI, obesity, anemia, and cancer in situ. Safety data note no suicide-risk flag but incomplete contemporaneous risk assessment and limited detail on current functioning, sleep, pain, and cognitive status. A careful, patient-centered plan is warranted that re-evaluates PTSD severity and medical status, re-engages trauma-focused psychotherapy (preferably CPT with MST-informed supervision if acceptable to patient), and reviews pharmacotherapy with attention to geriatric/cardiac safety. Investigational psychedelic/ketamine options are not recommended as routine care given evidence limitations and cardiac risk. This plan emphasizes measurement-based care, safety planning, and coordinated medical and psychosocial care.

recommended_plan.text: Perform contemporaneous suicide risk assessment and document a safety plan; update baseline PTSD symptom profile with dates; obtain full medical status.
recommended_plan.rationale: Safety first; contemporaneous risk assessment and updated symptom/profile data are prerequisites for any treatment modification.

recommended_plan.text: Revisit traumatic-memory-focused care and discuss CPT resumption/booster sessions with a clinician experienced in MST and older adult care; document patient preferences and prior responder details.
recommended_plan.rationale: Prior CPT response suggests potential benefit from trauma-focused care; re-engagement should be collaborative and paced with patient preferences and medical safeguards.
cautions: Ensure MST-informed clinician availability; monitor for destabilization; tailor pacing to patient tolerance and cognitive status

recommended_plan.text: Coordinate with the prescribing clinician to reassess sertraline dose, duration, adherence, tolerability, and symptom response by cluster; consider optimization only with medical clearance and shared decision-making.
recommended_plan.rationale: SSRIs remain first-line pharmacotherapy for PTSD; sertraline requires careful dosing/monitoring in older adults with cardiac disease.
cautions: Cardiac comorbidity risk (QT prolongation potential, orthostatic effects)
Falls risk; drug interactions; hyponatremia risk in older adults

recommended_plan.text: Defer psychedelic- or ketamine-assisted interventions outside approved research settings; if discussed, ensure formal risk-benefit discussion and specialist oversight.
recommended_plan.rationale: Psychedelic- and ketamine-assisted therapies are investigational and not routine care for PTSD in this patient; any discussion should occur within a research framework with appropriate oversight.
cautions: Research status; ensure informed consent if discussing investigational options

recommended_plan.text: Implement structured outcome monitoring using PCL-5 (with baseline date) and schedule follow-up assessments at defined intervals; align with functional goals and coordinate with primary care/cardiology.
recommended_plan.rationale: Systematic outcome measurement supports goal-directed treatment adjustments and safety monitoring.
cautions: Ensure baseline dates are captured and standardized administration

recommended_plan.text: Coordinate logistics and access (transport, telehealth, caregiver involvement) and consider geriatric psychiatry or MST-focused services as available; ensure cardiovascular status is considered in all psychotropic decisions.
recommended_plan.rationale: Integrating medical and psychosocial care reduces risk and improves adherence in complex cases.

monitoring: PTSD symptom tracking with PCL-5 and/or CAPS-5 at defined intervals; document baseline date
Safety monitoring for suicidality, protective factors, and a formal safety plan
Medication safety monitoring for sertraline (dose, adherence, adverse effects) and cardiovascular interactions
Monitoring of sleep quality, nightmares, pain, daytime functioning and cognition
Treatment engagement and feasibility of CPT booster sessions; assess access barriers (transport, telehealth)
reassessment_triggers: Emergence or escalation of suicidality or self-harm risk
Worsening PTSD symptoms or functional impairment despite treatment
Adverse cardiac events, new cardiac symptoms, or medications impacting psych care
Non-adherence to medications or psychotherapy; patient requests alternative approaches
Lack of clinically meaningful improvement after 6–8 weeks of therapy or pharmacotherapy optimization
New medical contraindications or drug interactions requiring urgent review
missing: Contemporary suicide risk assessment and safety plan documentation
Dates and method for current PTSD symptom assessments (PCL-5/CAPS-5) and functional impairment baseline
Detailed CPT history (course length, responder criteria, residual symptoms, patient preferences)
Current sertraline dose, duration, adherence, tolerability, and interactions; need cardiology/geriatric safety clearance
Updated medical status related to cardiac disease (recent imaging/results), sleep disturbances, pain, cognition, and falls risk
Patient preferences for therapy modality, anticipated barriers to access (transport, telehealth, caregiver involvement) and consent status
